STARLI | FLAGSHIP 13 FISSION Ten Research Design Monographs | Flagships 141-150 / 300 Author: 33 | White Rainbow Epoch | Research Design Working Edition v1.2 This ten-volume STARLI series examines trustworthy AI-assisted micro/nanorobotic experiments and nano-quantum measurement systems. The common research question is how to bind physical observation, decision authority, calibration uncertainty, and independently reconstructable evidence without mistaking computational confidence for experimental proof. Each volume is a 777-page English, nonclinical prospective research design containing 30 mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 separately paginated research studies, 200 Research Gates with six mechanistic annotations, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Across the ten volumes, the collection contains 300 research plates, 820 chapters, 4,100 study pages, 2,000 Research Gates, and 330 Phoenix candidates. Research scope by flagship F141 | Microrobotic Autonomous Control Authority Envelope at the Limit — Defines physical authority envelopes for microrobotic control, including credential expiry, actuator veto, permission transfer, and independently observed safe stopping. F142 | AI Nano-Quantum System Trustworthy Refusal Decision at the Limit — Studies when an AI-guided nano-quantum system must refuse action, separating calibrated abstention from indiscriminate rejection and unsafe confidence. F143 | Microscale Autonomous Experimental Design at the Limit — Examines autonomous microscale experimental design under specimen, information, energy, and permission budgets, with causal identification and independent replication. F144 | AI Quantum Sensing Uncertainty Calibration at the Limit — Investigates calibration of quantum-sensing uncertainty, including shared drift, covariance, phase ambiguity, photon budgets, and fair classical comparisons. F145 | Nanorobotic Closed-Loop Control Replayability at the Limit — Tests whether nanorobotic closed-loop decisions can be replayed from raw sensor data, actuator histories, calibration versions, and unselected failures. F146 | AI-Driven Microscale Active Sampling at the Limit — Designs AI-driven active sampling experiments that jointly measure analyte recovery, physical disturbance, resource cost, and contamination under blinded controls. F147 | Nano-Quantum System Human Review Mechanism at the Limit — Evaluates human review of nano-quantum decisions through signed authority, contradictory permissions, case-level uncertainty, and independent physical vetoes. F148 | AI Autonomous Research Agent Safety Boundary at the Limit — Defines safety boundaries for autonomous research agents across instrument access, sample authorization, unsafe tool composition, and immutable evidence. F149 | Microrobotic Autonomous System Interlaboratory Generalization at the Limit — Tests transfer of frozen microrobotic protocols between laboratories with different geometries, materials, calibration trees, operators, and failure environments. F150 | AI Nano-Quantum Trustworthy Autonomous Laboratory at the Limit — Integrates sample custody, microrobotic actuation, quantum/classical readouts, controlled autonomy, human oversight, and cross-site evidence reconstruction. Scientific boundary and publication status These books provide falsifiable research questions, candidate mathematical models, prospective blinded tests, competing explanations, negative-result criteria, and successor research interfaces. They do not report performed experiments or establish clinical efficacy, autonomous deployment safety, or quantum advantage. Independent expert verification of physical assumptions, formula applicability, all bibliographic relationships, and the scientific independence of closely related designs remains necessary. STARLI / RESEARCH FAMILY III / FLAGSHIPS 281–285 Ten Research Flagships · Letters to Future Laboratories Five research architectures for calibration succession, automated discovery, collaboration, self-repair and quantum sensor recovery. F281 | NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH SYSTEM CROSS-GENERATION CALIBRATION AT THE LIMIT Three-coupling: long-horizon scientific memory × traceable calibration and reference transfer × intergenerational evidence transfer. The primary proposal tests measurement unit definition survival under a concealed challenge: swap a noncommutable reference standard. Measures: reference-transfer bias [nT]; separate witness: uncertainty coverage [fraction]. Strong comparator: independent reference magnetometry with fixed calibration transfer. Failures remain reportable. F282 | INTELLIGENT MICROROBOTIC AUTOMATED SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY AT THE LIMIT Three-coupling: long-horizon scientific memory × modular autonomous infrastructure × uncertainty-aware bounded decision. The primary proposal tests sequential experiment acquisition bias under a concealed challenge: change a microgripper contact force. Measures: held-out experiment information gain [bits]; separate witness: hypothesis replication success [fraction]. Strong comparator: randomized factorial design and classical active learning under matched budgets. Failures remain reportable. F283 | NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AGENT COLLABORATION AT THE LIMIT Three-coupling: long-horizon scientific memory × modular autonomous infrastructure × intergenerational evidence transfer. The primary proposal tests conflicting measurement ontology negotiation under a concealed challenge: corrupt one agent clock. Measures: causally valid agreement [fraction]; separate witness: external reconstruction success [fraction]. Strong comparator: single authorized controller with independent scientific adjudicator. Failures remain reportable. F284 | MICROSCALE RESEARCH PLATFORM AUTONOMOUS REPAIR AT THE LIMIT Three-coupling: long-horizon scientific memory × modular autonomous infrastructure × intergenerational evidence transfer. The primary proposal tests reference-sensor replacement after failure under a concealed challenge: mask a cleaning reagent carryover. Measures: verified restoration yield [fraction]; separate witness: post-repair alignment bias [um]. Strong comparator: manual maintenance under frozen physical qualification limits. Failures remain reportable. F285 | QUANTUM SENSOR RESOURCE CYCLING AND RECOVERY AT THE LIMIT Three-coupling: long-horizon scientific memory × modular autonomous infrastructure × intergenerational evidence transfer. The primary proposal tests microcoil solder fatigue under a concealed challenge: reuse a shield with unlogged hysteresis. Measures: sensor functional recovery [fraction]; separate witness: recovered component mass [mg]. Strong comparator: new-component replacement with matched metrology and life-cycle accounting. Failures remain reportable. FORMAT Each flagship: 777 English pages · 30 formula plates · 82 chapters / 410 one-page investigations · 200 three-letter Research Gates · 33 Phoenix proposals. All assertions are candidate research designs, not experimental outcomes.
